background.method: Launch a fresh native-only fixture process without React, the SDK or its lifecycle observer. Foreground Settings. After the real UIKit background notification returns, initialize the first React/SDK runtime on the main queue while UIKit is still Background. Require the cached raw native first-initialization state and current native process state to be background, zero subscription starts and no delivery during the observation window, then foreground the same process and receive the peer message through the same reader.
background.limitation: This proves fresh React/SDK initialization in real OS background. It does not prove APNs delivery, system-triggered cold OS process launch, or execution on a physical device. The private phase name cold-background is retained in the raw report and does not expand this scope.

reloadSettlementWitness.behavior: After releasing the old signer, runtime/observe waits for its fulfilled/rejected result and the actual old HTTP response finish/close event, then waits a two-second stale-call observation window. Installed runtime success requires fulfilled signer, terminal HTTP disposition, the completed window and staleCalls=0. A closed old request is a valid transport cancellation witness; it is not native callback drain. Final conformance /result admission independently calls the controller gate again, requiring completed successful observation and the current staleCalls=0, including callbacks arriving after the observation returned.
tests: Real HTTP request cancelled before the old signer resolves: observation cannot report unsettled signer as safe.
Real HTTP signature response finishes; a stale continuation arrives 100ms later and is counted by the post-settlement window.
Final result is rejected before/during observation and after a late stale call; it is accepted only after successful observation.
reloadSettlementWitness.limits: Control tests prove the actual HTTP gate and delayed-callback sensitivity. All four current canonical installed Hermes conformance reports passed runtime-reload, in addition to the recorded historical bare iOS run. Neither proves native callback drain or excludes callbacks after the bounded two-second window.
